_readme: Confirmed address->meaning mappings for VSHELL.EXE / DBSIM.EXE, extracted from
Herculan/docs/formats/*.md, docs/simulation/*.md, and the
project_es2_exe_recon memory file. Applied to the Ghidra project by
ES2ApplySymbolNames.java (tools/ghidra_scripts/). Re-run that script after adding
entries here -- it is idempotent.
Fields per entry:
address     - hex address, no '0x' prefix (e.g. '00411fc4')
binary      - 'VSHELL' or 'DBSIM' (must match the -process file name at apply time)
type        - 'function' or 'data'
confidence  - 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
name        - proposed symbol name. OMITTED for 'low' confidence entries -- those get
a plate comment only, never a rename/label, so a guess can never look like
a confirmed name in the database. 'medium' confidence names are prefixed
'maybe_' by convention (kept explicit here rather than inferred from
confidence, so the apply script does no string-editing of names).
description - short evidence/meaning note, safe to also use as the plate comment body.
source      - repo doc or memory section this was extracted from, for traceability.
Confidence guide (see Herculan docs for full evidence per entry):
high   - verified via multiple cross-checks (raw disassembly, byte-exact match against
real files, or explicit 'confirmed'/'solved' language in the source doc).
medium - a reasoned, plausible finding ('very likely', 'best guess', 'plausibly') that
was NOT independently cross-checked. Renamed with a maybe_ prefix, never bare.
low    - open/unconfirmed ('unknown', 'not yet observed', 'meaning not confirmed').
Comment only, no rename.
Struct-instance offsets (e.g. 'mech+0x222' for the shield struct) are deliberately NOT
included here -- they aren't fixed Ghidra addresses, so they'd need a proper structure
data type to label meaningfully, which is out of scope for this file/script.

entries.name: LoadWeaponsDat
entries.description: File-level parser for gam\weapons.dat (SHELL0/GAM weapon catalog, 33 entries). Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: LoadHercsDat
entries.description: Loads gam\hercs.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: LoadHercInfDat
entries.description: Loads gam\herc_inf.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: LoadCareerDat
entries.description: Loads gam\career.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: LoadDamageDat_Shell
entries.description: Loads gam\damage.dat -- VSHELL/UI-facing summary table (fixed 9x{6,9} shorts + 0x21 shorts), distinct from DBSIM's variable per-Herc hit-zone table loaded by HercPiece_LoadTable. Confirmed via direct string reference.

entries.name: Volume_LoadVolume
entries.description: Volume::loadVolume. Confirmed via matching Class::method assert string ('VolRStream revision' mismatch check) and clean decompile after the parameter-commit fix.

entries.name: WeaponsDat_ReadRecord
entries.description: Per-record body reader for WEAPONS.DAT (29-byte stride, blockLen-prefixed front block, price field at 0x14 scaled x1000). Called from LoadWeaponsDat.

entries.name: WeaponsBin_LookupName
entries.description: Bounds-checked weapon-name lookup into weapons.bin by weapon id (offsets[id] + stringPoolStart). Structure verified byte-exact against the real retail file in ES2/VOL/LANG0.VOL.

entries.name: WeaponsBin_Open
entries.description: Opens weapons.bin by its literal filename string found in VSHELL.EXE.

entries.name: WeaponsDat_RecordArray
entries.description: In-memory WEAPONS.DAT record array, 29 bytes/record. Stride confirmed via IMUL EDX,EDX,0x1d in raw disassembly (FUN_0041266a), not decompiler pointer-math (which mis-implied 116 bytes).

entries.name: maybe_Armory_ItemCostCalc
entries.description: Reads WeaponsDat_RecordArray fields 0x14 (price, /1000) and 0x17 (multiplier -- plausibly ammo/quantity count, not confirmed by a load-time read).

entries.name: maybe_Armory_TotalCostCalc
entries.description: Armory total-cost calculation; sums the price field (0x14) as a direct per-item cost contribution.
A 2-byte value per weapon id, stored in a separate parallel array from the 29-byte WeaponsDat_RecordArray record at load time. Meaning not confirmed.

entries.name: maybe_WeaponsBinFileHandle
entries.description: weapons.bin's stream/file handle, referenced alongside WeaponsDat_RecordArray in the WEAPONS.DAT loading call chain.

entries.name: Msn_BuildPath
entries.description: Builds the msn\<name>.msn path string (format 'msn\\%s.msn', with '^' sanitized to '_') before loading a mission.

entries.name: MsnGen_LoadMission
entries.description: msn_gen.cpp. Calls MsnGen_ParseMsnFile (00417b67) first with the .msn path, then WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54) -- confirmed to be data\script.dat's writer, serializing a GUID-filtered field-subset re-export of the same in-memory row arrays MsnGen_ParseMsnFile just populated. See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: MsnGen_ParseMsnFile
entries.description: The raw .MSN byte parser (msn_gen.cpp). Revision-field check, scratch/patch pass, then 17 record-array rows with a condition-filter/template-inheritance system. Macro-structure confirmed byte-exact against 61/62 real retail .MSN files.

entries.name: WriteScriptDatFile
entries.description: Fully traced: the WRITER of data\script.dat. Serializes directly from the same in-memory .msn row-array globals FUN_00417b67 populates (DAT_0047064e/0x16=row6, DAT_00470650/10=row7, DAT_00470656=row8, DAT_0047065e/0xc=row9, DAT_00470660/0x52=row10, DAT_00470662/0x1e=row11, DAT_00470652/0x90=row12, DAT_00470654/0x66=row13, DAT_0047065c/0x3e=row14, DAT_00470658/0x16=row15, DAT_0047065a/0xa4=row16, DAT_0047064a/0x3a=row17, DAT_00470640=row4), filtering out GUID==-1 (deleted/inactive) records per row and exporting only a field subset of each. See docs/formats/script-dat.md for the full block table.

entries.name: ShellMap_Constructor
entries.description: ShellMap::ctor (vtable &PTR_FUN_004721b0). Opens data\mission.str and data\maplabel.str as independent string tables, then calls ShellMap_LoadScriptDat. Confirmed via assert string.

entries.name: ShellMap_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. VSHELL's own map-editor reader for data\script.dat -- a SECOND, independent reader of the same 13-block structure WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54, VSHELL) writes and DBSim_LoadScriptDat (00424308, DBSIM) also reads. Confirmed byte-for-byte identical block order/strides to both, differing only in which fields it keeps vs seeks past (e.g. keeps row12/row14/row15 blocks in full for UI display, where DBSIM keeps only 1 field or discards entirely). NOT an independent/map-rendering-only format -- that was an earlier, since-corrected guess. See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: maybe_Career_SaveSlotCopyA
entries.description: career.cpp. Part of the confirmed save-slot handoff copy mechanism (sav\script%d.dat<->data\script.dat, sav\missn%d.str<->data\mission.str, sav\player%d.mec<->data\player.mec) -- which specific direction/pair this function handles wasn't individually pinned down.

entries.name: maybe_Career_SaveSlotCopyB
entries.description: career.cpp. Part of the confirmed save-slot handoff copy mechanism -- see maybe_Career_SaveSlotCopyA.

entries.name: maybe_CampaignFlagArray
entries.description: Global flag/counter array compared against by the .MSN condition/trigger opcode system (switch 0x119-0x11e: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=). 'Almost certainly' the campaign-progress flag store the original Java doc predicted but never located -- not independently cross-checked against a known campaign flag.

entries.name: Msn_ConditionFilterGate
entries.description: Shared condition-filter helper used by every .MSN record array; compacts an array in place based on campaign state, implementing the 0x119-0x11e comparison opcodes against maybe_CampaignFlagArray.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveGuidToIndex
entries.description: GUID-based search/resolve into an already-loaded .MSN record array by stable authored id (search-only mode also used as an insert-or-merge key check). Confirmed via a 100% (275/275) match rate resolving row #10's sub-refs against row #9's GUIDs.

entries.name: maybe_Msn_ResolveRow6Ref
entries.description: Resolves a short field into row #6's index space -- used by row #9 (LinkOrReward12)'s 0x08/0x0A ref fields.

entries.name: maybe_Msn_ApplyScratchPatch
entries.description: Applies effects during the one-shot 82-byte scratch pass in MsnGen_ParseMsnFile (a reused buffer, not a persistent entity array) -- looks like a campaign-override/patch application, not confirmed further.

entries.name: Math_Q8Multiply
entries.description: Q8 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 8. Verified via raw disassembly (SHRD EAX,EDX,0x8) matching the decompiler's >>8 exactly.

entries.name: Math_IntegrateRateOverTick
entries.description: Q8mul(SimTickDelta, rate), clamped to signed 16-bit range. Core 'apply a per-unit-time rate as this tick's delta' primitive.

entries.name: Math_CountdownTimerTick
entries.description: *timerPtr -= SimTickDelta, clamped to 0, returns the new value. Used for cooldowns (e.g. the rocket seeker's target-reacquire timer).

entries.name: Math_RateLimitedMoveToward
entries.description: Generic per-tick turn/slew-rate limiter: moves current toward target by at most step, returns remaining error. Used by rocket guidance and the shield recharge tick.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 3D magnitude approximation: L + M*0.34375 + S*0.25 (sorted |dx|,|dy|,|dz|). Verified via raw disassembly (three CMP/XCHG sort pairs, SAR+ADD coefficient chains). Reused for collision bounding-sphere radius and rocket proximity-fuze range checks.

entries.name: SimTickDelta
entries.description: Global simulation timestep, read (never written) by the fixed-point math toolkit. Confirms DBSIM runs a discrete fixed/semi-fixed timestep simulation.

entries.name: Collision_RegisterObject
entries.description: collide.cpp. Top-level collision-model entry point: allocates the next slot in the fixed collision-object table, then calls Collision_LoadRecordArray.

entries.name: Collision_LoadRecordArray
entries.description: Reads a collision record count, allocates count*10 bytes, loads each via Collision_LoadSubSpheres then post-processes via Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere.

entries.name: Collision_LoadSubSpheres
entries.description: Reads a per-record sub-sphere count, calls Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag per sub-sphere.

entries.name: Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag
entries.description: Reads a sub-sphere flag byte; if set, calls Collision_LoadSubMeshIndices.

entries.name: Collision_LoadSubMeshIndices
entries.description: Reads a 13-bit-masked packed count+flags field and, if nonzero, loads that many 8-byte index/sub-mesh records.

entries.name: Collision_ComputeBoundingSphere
entries.description: Builds a record's bounding sphere from child spheres: AABB of inflated children, center = AABB midpoint, radius = Math_FastMagnitude3D of the half-extents.

entries.name: Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided
entries.description: rocket.cpp. Loads the Type-0 rocket type table (14-byte/0xe stride, confirmed via IMUL-style indexing).

entries.name: Rocket_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: RocketType* getType() accessor: RocketTypeTable + instance.typeIndex(byte @ +0x41) * 0xe.

entries.name: Rocket_Fire
entries.description: Spawn ('fire a rocket') entry point. Constructs via Missile_Construct or Rocket_ConstructGuided, captures lock-on target once at launch.

entries.name: Missile_Construct
entries.description: Constructs the Type-0/unguided rocket-family object. PROJ.DAT category 0 (5 entries, real Speed, armor>>shield, uniform SplashFactor=500).

entries.name: Rocket_ConstructGuided
entries.description: Constructs the Type-3/guided rocket-family object (own type table). PROJ.DAT category 3 (3 entries, shield==armor exactly).

entries.name: Bullet_Construct
entries.description: Constructs the Type-2 Bullet-class object (own vtable PTR_FUN_00498628, own 14-byte type table). PROJ.DAT category 2; MissileId 9 is the confirmed Plasma cannon.

entries.name: Rocket_TickUpdate
entries.description: Per-tick rocket update: seeker-slot reacquire, burnout check, integrate motion (damped speed update), homing-vs-ballistic dispatch, proximity-fuze warning check (<40000 units).

entries.name: Rocket_HomingSteer
entries.description: Lead-predicted homing/steering: LOS delta to extrapolated target position, deadband (+/-0xc00 inside +/-0x1800), rate-limited turn (0x500/tick cap via Math_RateLimitedMoveToward).

entries.name: Rocket_BallisticSteer
entries.description: Non-homing steering variant: takes the launcher's one-shot aim-point delta directly, no deadband/rate-limiting, clears the aim-point fields after consuming them.

entries.name: Bullet_TickUpdate
entries.description: bullet.cpp per-bullet-instance tick. Fixed age rate Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(0x200). type==9 branch (confirmed Plasma cannon, MissileId 9 on a Bullet instance) calls Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep directly with a 4000-unit blast radius.

entries.name: Bullet_FireBurst
entries.description: Fire-burst/tracer spawner. Calls Sim_RaycastObjectList synchronously at fire time to resolve the hit before any tracer visual spawns -- this is the beam/hitscan (PROJ.DAT Type 4, always Speed=0) mechanism: no persisting travelling object.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_Missile
entries.description: Missile-capable-hardpoint fire dispatcher: checks the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type field, Type==Missile(0) -> Rocket_Fire, else falls through to the shared Bullet fallback.

entries.name: WeaponMount_FireDispatch_GunBeam
entries.description: Gun/beam-capable-hardpoint fire dispatcher: checks the mount's cached PROJ.DAT Type field, Type==4(Beam) -> Bullet_FireBurst (instant), else unconditionally constructs a Type=2 Bullet object.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecord
entries.description: PROJ.DAT in-memory lookup by (category, subtypeId) -- linear search against ProjDat_RecordTable.

entries.name: Weapons_LoadResourceTables
entries.description: Opens 'wpntex' (textures), 'mechwpn2', 'weapons' (88-byte per-hardpoint mount-template records), then 'proj' -- reads PROJ.DAT's 36-byte records into ProjDat_RecordTable. Previously flagged as a 'zero callers, dead end' before being decompiled -- it is not a dead end. The 'weapons' resource IS simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT -- confirmed byte-exact (2026-08-11): reads a UINT16 Total then Total records via WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord, consuming exactly the file's full content length with zero remainder across all 33 real records.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_ReadRecord
entries.description: Per-record reader for simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT, called from Weapons_LoadResourceTables in a Total-length loop. Reuses HercPiece_ReadRecord (8-byte front + conditional dependent list) and Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag/Collision_LoadSubMeshIndices (2+2 bytes, then a variable count*8-byte array -- a per-weapon firing/mount-offset sequence, not real collision geometry) verbatim from the .DMG/.COL loaders, then a final raw 48-byte (0x30) block. Byte-exact verified: this exact read sequence consumes the real file's full 3790 content bytes across 33 records with zero remainder. Full writeup in docs/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: ProjDat_RecordTable
entries.description: PROJ.DAT's in-memory record table, 36 bytes/record, keyed by (category, subtypeId). Verified byte-exact against the real retail ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/PROJ.DAT (27 records) -- independently converges with the pre-existing C# ProjectileData.cs field layout.

entries.name: maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided
entries.description: Type-0 rocket type table, 14-byte stride, loaded by Rocket_LoadTypeTable_Unguided.

entries.name: maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided_Count
entries.description: Record count for maybe_RocketTypeTable_Unguided.

entries.name: Terrain_LoadZone
entries.description: terrain.cpp zone/grid loader. Builds a 'zoneNNNN' filename, reads a grid header, allocates a HeightGrid, installs it as ActiveHeightGrid.

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQuery
entries.description: Converts world (x,y) to a grid cell, fetches 4 corner texels from a 16-byte-per-cell heightmap, does proper barycentric/bilinear interpolation across a per-cell-selectable diagonal (2-bit flag per cell).

entries.name: ActiveHeightGrid
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-installed HeightGrid struct, confirmed set by Terrain_LoadZone.

entries.name: maybe_Flyer_TerrainAvoidanceAutopilot
entries.description: Six direction-flag-gated sensor probes (front/back/left/right/up/down) nudging vertical speed and playing a distance-scaled alarm tone. Best-guess home TU flyersys.cpp, not proven by a direct assert string.

entries.name: Sim_RaycastObjectList
entries.description: Generic ray-vs-live-object-list query. Exactly 5 confirmed call sites: rocket homing, bullet tick/burst, and the flyer terrain-avoidance autopilot. Calls each candidate's vtable +0x20 (hit-test) and +0x50 (AI threat-tracking).

entries.name: maybe_Mech_AiThreatTracking
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x50, called per raycast candidate by Sim_RaycastObjectList. AI threat-tracking/target-acquisition update ('this object just took fire'), confirmed NOT a damage function.

entries.name: Mech_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x20. Range check -> Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire -> Mech_SelectStruckComponent -> Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage. The hit-test and damage application are the same call, one level deeper than Sim_RaycastObjectList's caller.

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire
entries.description: Direct-fire shield absorption: picks front/rear zone by hit side, absorbed = min(incomingDamage, remainingShieldInZone), hard cap not threshold gate.

entries.name: Mech_SelectStruckComponent
entries.description: Deterministic single-component selection via real hit geometry -- iterates up to 29 component slots, tracks best match, returns exactly the one struck (no randomness, unlike the explosive path).

entries.name: Mech_ComponentGeometryTest_Candidate
entries.description: Per-candidate coarse geometry test, called by Mech_SelectStruckComponent.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage
entries.description: Applies a per-weapon-type Q8 multiplier (Math_Q8Multiply(shotData+8, damage)), splits the result between destroying the struck weapon mount (possible secondary explosion via mech vtable +0x70) and general component health via mech vtable +0x74.

entries.name: Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep
entries.description: Radius-based splash-damage entry point. Sweeps the live-object list; distance-hitRadius<blastRadius calls each object's +0x70 vtable damage method. Exactly 3 confirmed call sites, all genuinely explosive/terminal (missile ground impact, Plasma-cannon bullet type 9, mech death) -- NOT a universal weapon-fire path.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyExplosiveDamage
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x70. Front/rear facing classification -> Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive -> ~51% per-component random roll across up to 29 slots -> linear distance falloff (overflow * (blastRadius-distance)/blastRadius) via mech vtable +0x74.

entries.name: Mech_ShieldAbsorb_Explosive
entries.description: Explosion path's own separate shield-absorption implementation (parallel to, not shared with, Mech_ShieldAbsorb_DirectFire). scaledDamage=(weaponDamage*1000)>>8, clamps zone to 0, returns scaled overflow.

entries.name: Rocket_GroundImpactDetonate
entries.description: Checks altitude vs. terrain height every tick via Terrain_HeightQuery; on ground contact calls Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep(pos, 3000, 10000, 0, null).

entries.name: Mech_DeathExplosion
entries.description: Mech death/destruction handler. One Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep splash call, then unconditionally applies a flat 32000 damage to every remaining component (guaranteed-destruction cleanup, no roll/falloff).

entries.name: Mech_ComponentHealthWrite
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x74. Shared health-write/cascade endpoint for both damage pathways. 8-level percentage bucketing with alert sounds, leg-pair status tracking (dependent-array slots {0,1} front legs, {10,11} rear legs on 4-legged types), mech-death trigger on enough destroyed limbs.

entries.name: Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade
entries.description: Subtracts damage from a component's current value (via a helper); if the component crosses into 'destroyed', cascades via Component_DestroyAndCascade.

entries.name: Component_DestroyAndCascade
entries.description: Destroys a component (debris/effect index lookup, HUD slot state write) and walks the BoneId destruction-dependency group, destroying every sibling that shares the same BoneId.

entries.name: Component_ReadHealthPercent
entries.description: Reads a component's current/max as Q8 (0-256): aggregates the component's own value with all its dependent sub-components' current/max before computing (totalCurrent<<8)/totalMax.

entries.name: Component_AllocHealthArrays
entries.description: Allocates the header of pointers at mech+0x206: a 22-entry dependent health array, a 29-entry main component health array, and a 29-entry active-flag array (all zeroed except the flag array, filled 0x01).

entries.name: Component_LinkMaxRefData
entries.description: Wires up mech+0x212 (and neighboring fields) as a pointer into per-component maximum/reference data, sourced from the mech's own .DMG-derived pointer plus its Collision_RegisterObject registration record.

entries.name: HercPiece_ReadRecord
entries.description: Loads one 18-byte .DMG HercPiece record: max health, debris-flags index pair, BoneId (bone/destruction-group key), DestructionFlags bitfield, dependent sub-component list pointer+count.

entries.name: HercPiece_LoadTable
entries.description: Loads the .DMG per-mech component table: a count-prefixed flat byte array followed by a count-prefixed array of 18-byte HercPiece records (via HercPiece_ReadRecord).

entries.name: Damage_LoadMechDmgFile
entries.description: damage.cpp dispatch/setup that opens dmg\[herc].DMG (filename built from the mech's own name string) and drives HercPiece_LoadTable. Called from the mech constructor.

entries.name: Mech_Constructor
entries.description: The Mech class constructor -- assigns a fully-populated 34-slot vtable at 0x0049a282 (by far the largest of the base-constructor-helper's 13 callers). Calls Damage_LoadMechDmgFile, Shield_Init, Component_AllocHealthArrays, Component_LinkMaxRefData.

entries.name: maybe_ComponentDependencyList
entries.description: Dependency list walked by Component_DestroyAndCascade to find and destroy dependent components.

entries.name: Shield_Init
entries.description: Initializes the 5-field shield struct (mech+0x222) from the mech-type base capacity (typeRecord+0xc0): max fields = baseValue, current fields = baseValue>>1 (default 50/50 split).

entries.name: Mech_GetShieldByHeading
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x34. Given a heading angle, returns the front (+0x222) or rear (+0x224) shield value by which side is within +/-90 degrees.

entries.name: Sim_MainTick
entries.description: DBSIM's per-frame simulation tick. Updates SimTickDelta from a hardware/timer source, iterates every global object list, and calls Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate once per live mech in GlobalMechList.

entries.name: Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate
entries.description: Per-mech-per-tick reactor/energy bookkeeping (integrates reactor output rate into the energy pool at +0x292), then dispatches weapon-energy arbitration and shield-recharge via Shield_RechargeTick.

entries.name: Shield_RechargeTick
entries.description: Shield recharge primitive: clamps the request to at most 5 units/tick and to the remaining deficit, redistributes front/rear via balance using Math_RateLimitedMoveToward, returns the unclaimed portion.

entries.name: Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate
entries.description: Called once per frame for LocalPlayerMech only, from the main-loop function. Cockpit/HUD-adjacent bookkeeping; calls Shield_BalanceInputRead among other things.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceInputRead
entries.description: Reads the shield-balance HUD gauge widget's click state; if a flag is set, calls Shield_BalanceAdjust. Also pushes front/rear display percentages back to the widget.

entries.name: Shield_BalanceAdjust
entries.description: Nudges the shield balance field (mech+0x226) by +/-0x66 (102), clamped to [0, 0x400] (0-1024). Default center 0x200 (512).

entries.name: Mech_ConfigureLoadout
entries.description: Mech loadout (re)configuration, called on spawn/equip changes. Allocates the weapon-mount-manager object at mech+0x202 (malloc 0x14 or 0x35 bytes depending on the 'locally-simulated' flag).

entries.name: LocalPlayerMech
entries.description: Confirmed global pointer to 'this instance's own locally-piloted mech' -- set in the level-init function by scanning the mech list for the one with the locally-simulated flag set.

entries.name: GlobalMechList
entries.description: Global list of live mechs, walked once per tick by Sim_MainTick (calling Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate per live, non-removed, non-dead mech).

entries.name: maybe_GlobalLiveObjectList
entries.description: Global live-object list walked by Sim_RaycastObjectList and Damage_ExplosiveBlastSweep. Shared with confirmed objlist.cpp functions, not proven by a direct assert-string tie to Sim_RaycastObjectList itself.

entries.name: ClassItem_LoadResource
entries.description: Generic polymorphic resource loader entry point (stream, mode). Reads an 8-byte type tag via ClassItem_ReadTypeTag, looks up a handler via ClassItem_FindHandler, calls its loadFn.

entries.name: ClassItem_ReadTypeTag
entries.description: Reads the 8-byte type tag from a resource stream, called by ClassItem_LoadResource.

entries.name: ClassItem_FindHandler
entries.description: Searches a registry of (idArray, count) bucket pairs for a matching type tag, returns a 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} descriptor.

entries.name: Panel_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DFN/.HFN panel loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the panel's filename.

entries.name: Cursor_LoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DCI cursor loads into ClassItem_LoadResource with the cursor's filename.

entries.name: Gau_Load
entries.description: PANEL.CPP's confirmed .GAU loader. Allocates a 1700-byte (0x6a4) struct -- matching .GAU's confirmed content size exactly -- then constructs 6 sub-widgets via vector-new, the first matching .GAU's confirmed weapon-slot layout (offset 20, count 10, stride 16).

entries.name: Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets
entries.description: Caller of Gau_Load. Builds a per-herc cockpit object and constructs 7 top-level HUD widgets from fixed literal byte offsets (468, 548, 616, 728, 1000, 1088, 1212) into the loaded .GAU struct.

entries.name: Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 468 widget wrapper -> FUN_00441dd0: container for the Weapon Chain-select/Link/Auto-track button gadgets (4 children from offsets 484/500/516/532).

entries.name: Gau_EnergyMeterWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 548 widget wrapper -> FUN_00444d5c: container for the Energy Meter widget (1 child from offset 564).

entries.name: Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 616 widget wrapper -> FUN_004434fc: Shield Display's front/rear numeric value label widgets (children at 632/648/664/680), nested inside the confirmed HShieldDisplay byte range.

entries.name: Gau_MfdPanelWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 728 widget wrapper -> FUN_00445218: the MFD's actual interactive behavior -- mode-switching state machine, radar-sweep table, damage-readout digits. Behavior behind the confirmed HMfdPanel bounding box at 952.

entries.name: Gau_ThrottleWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 1000 widget wrapper -> FUN_00447b84: the Throttle widget (already fully confirmed/ported in the C# port).

entries.name: Gau_RovingGunsightWrapper
entries.description: .GAU offset 1088 widget wrapper, constructs the roving-gunsight complex via Gau_RovingGunsightWidget.

entries.name: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget
entries.description: Large composite 'roving gunsight' HUD-overlay container (matches HUDRovingGunsightGadget/HUDLockingGunsight/HUDPipper class names). Contains the confirmed HTorsoTwist (child rect at 1104, loads bitmap 'hudhtick') and a target-speed text-readout anchor (offsets 1120/1124/1132, format string '000 K/H'). NAVBAR is confirmed NOT here.

entries.name: Gau_PilotRosterWidget
entries.description: .GAU offset 1212 widget wrapper -> FUN_00448cc8: pilot-roster/crew-status HDD readout ('hddclip'/'pilots'/'static' strings), constructs 15 sub-widgets, accounts for the remainder of GAUFile.Remainder (roughly bytes 1212-1588).

entries.name: DBSim_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: DBSIM's reader for data\script.dat, called from World::ctor-equivalent init path (also opens player.mec and mission.str at nearby offsets). Reads a fixed 20-byte header into DAT_004a9ed2 and uses it twice: World_LoadTheater(&header) takes the int16 at 0 as the theater and the int16 at 18 as its variant, and Terrain_LoadZone(header[2]) takes the int16 at 2 as THE ZONE INDEX -- verified against all ten retail script.dat files, every offset-2 value is a zone that ships. It also zeroes the field at offset 4 before use. Then 13 count-prefixed blocks in exact order matching VSHELL's WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54): row6-coords(12B), row7-heading(2B, x0xb6 degrees->BAM), row8-nested-waypoints, row9(6B), row10-Action82(74B read, only 1 field of the row10-referencing sub-block reused), row11-ActionPair30(24B, resolved via FUN_00423104), row12(134B raw, only the mech-type-ref field at rec-offset 40 kept), row13(92B raw, only rec-offset 44 field kept), row14(52B raw, only the type field kept), row15(14B, read and fully discarded), row16(156B, nested 20-entry crossref with a 3-way discriminator that marks row6/row7/row14 slots 'live' -- this is DBSIM's actual entity-activation mechanism), row17(54B, read and fully discarded), then a final flat count+array tail = row4's populated LUT-ref prefix (the mission's herc/weapon unlock package). See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildActionPairRecord
entries.description: Small helper called once per row11 (ActionPair30) record inside DBSim_LoadScriptDat: builds a resolved in-memory record from a target ref + a type/verb short + a 10-slot ref array, all already resolved to row10-array pointers by the caller.

entries.name: Widget_AllocZeroed
entries.description: Generic widget allocator: bounds-checks param_1 (a struct byte-size, e.g. 0x61/0x55/0x47/0x69/0x75/0x6e8 for different widget classes) against a fixed pool, allocates via FUN_004078e7, zeroes with memset, returns the block. No file/resource access -- confirms widget construction throughout VSHELL's tab screens is purely in-memory, not resource-indexed.

entries.name: maybe_Widget_InitRect
entries.description: Thin widget-init wrapper: calls base-init FUN_0040a6f4(widget, parent, rectPtr, ...)/Panel_Ctor to copy a caller-supplied {x,y,w,h} rect into the widget struct, then sets its own vtable pointer (0x61-byte struct) and clears a couple of state fields. Sibling wrappers over the same Panel_Ctor/Window_Ctor base are now individually disambiguated by their own vtable+paint-function pairs -- see Text_Ctor/Button_Ctor/ButtonIcon_Ctor/TitledPanel_Ctor/FramedPanel_Ctor/Grid_Ctor/HatchedDivider_Ctor/Panel_Ctor below. This one's own paint function (FUN_0040b772) wasn't independently decompiled/confirmed, so it stays medium/generic.

entries.name: Window_Ctor
entries.description: Lowest-level widget base constructor (window.cpp-equivalent). Sets a placeholder vtable (&PTR_FUN_004717dc, classic Watcom base-subobject-under-construction pattern), zeroes state fields, calls FUN_0041eb5c(widget, parent, rectPtr, style) to install the {x,y,w,h} rect (fields at +0x25/+0x29/+0x2d/+0x31 = left/top/right/bottom) and attach to the parent's child tree, then sets the real base vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046e828). Called by every other widget constructor, directly or via Control_Ctor.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Control_Ctor
entries.description: Mid-level widget base (wwinbase.cpp/esdialog.cpp-equivalent), one level above Window_Ctor: calls Window_Ctor, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046e810), zeroes an icon/style field at +0x45, ORs style flags 0x60 into the +0x39 flags word, sets +0x49=1 (default-visible), then calls Widget_ShowRecursive to cascade the show/attach notification down the tree. This is the base every 'has visible chrome' widget (Text, Button, Panel-family) constructs through, distinct from the plain-rect InitRect variant which skips it.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Widget_ShowRecursive
entries.description: Recursive show/attach cascade: sets the +0x11 'attached' state bit, recurses into every child (+0xd child-list head, +5 sibling-next) not already attached, then posts a type=2 event (via a small event-record alloc + FUN_00468440 dispatch) targeting the widget. Mirror of Widget_HideRecursive.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Widget_HideRecursive
entries.description: Recursive hide/detach cascade: clears the +0x11 'attached'/'parent-shown' state bits, posts type=1 (self) and type=4 (parent-directed) events, then recurses over a z-order sibling list (+9 offset). Mirror of Widget_ShowRecursive.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Panel_Ctor
entries.description: Simplest visible-chrome widget: calls Control_Ctor, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ead0, 0x55 or 0x65-byte struct depending on caller), stores a style/color param at +0x4d, sets +0x51=1. Its paint function (Panel_Paint, FUN_0040a959) does nothing but a single flat-fill call (FUN_0040a726(widget,1)) -- confirms this is a plain flat-colour rectangle/background panel, used raw (no further subclass wrapper) wherever screens need an unadorned coloured rect.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Panel_Paint
entries.description: Panel_Ctor's paint override: single flat-fill call, no border/text/children drawing. Confirms Panel_Ctor is the plain flat-colour rectangle widget class.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Text_Ctor
entries.description: The Text/Label widget class (0xc9=201-byte struct, by far the most-constructed widget class in VSHELL's screens, 68 uses across the 6 tab screens alone -- consistent with 'every caption/value/button-label is one of these'). Calls Control_Ctor, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ec54), stores font id (+0x45) and alignment/style (+0xb5, seen as constant 0x29=41 everywhere), then calls Text_SetString to copy the caller's string into a fixed 100-char buffer. Also constructed internally as the embedded caption child of Button_Ctor/ButtonIcon_Ctor.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Text_SetString
entries.description: Text_Ctor's string-setter: stores font/style params, copies the caller's string into the widget's fixed 100-char buffer (asserts 'Message text is too long' if over 100 chars, per the src\esmsg.cpp assert string -- Text shares its overlong-string guard with the message-queue system), or clears/hides the widget if the string is null/empty.

entries.name: ButtonIcon_Ctor
entries.description: Button-with-icon widget class (0x69=105-byte struct, 17 uses). Passes a click-callback function pointer straight through the widget's base constructor (confirmed at the ServiceBay_BuildScreen call sites: per-weapon-slot handlers FUN_00439f2d/FUN_00439fdc/FUN_0043a0d8/etc, one per weapon-buy button, each ~0xfa/250 bytes apart matching the per-row screen layout). Also constructs an embedded Text_Ctor child sized to the widget's full client rect for the button's caption. Sets the +0x39 flags word's 0x200 bit (likely 'clickable'/'enabled').

entries.name: Button_Ctor
entries.description: Plain button widget class, no icon slot (0x5d=93-byte struct, 18 uses -- smaller than ButtonIcon_Ctor's 0x69). Same embedded-Text_Ctor-child pattern as ButtonIcon_Ctor for its caption, but via Panel_Ctor's base rather than passing a callback through Control_Ctor's base-init call directly.

entries.name: TitledPanel_Ctor
entries.description: Root/tab-panel widget class with title-bar chrome (0x75=117-byte struct, 10 uses). Always the FIRST widget constructed in every one of the six *_BuildScreen functions, sized to near-fullscreen, given a title string (weapon-catalog or hardcoded caption) -- this is each tab screen's own root window. Constructs an embedded Text_Ctor title child, calls Widget_ShowRecursive at the end. Its paint override (TitledPanel_Paint) draws a header strip with vertical column-divider lines, a checkerboard-dithered body background, and a border -- classic titled-groupbox chrome.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: TitledPanel_Paint
entries.description: TitledPanel_Ctor's paint override: fills a header strip (height from +0x59) with vertical divider lines if the header-divider flag is set, else (no title-bar variant) fills the whole body with a checkerboard/dithered pixel pattern; either way finishes with a 4-corner-tick + rectangle border draw. Confirms TitledPanel_Ctor is a bordered, optionally-titled groupbox/root-window chrome.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: FramedPanel_Ctor
entries.description: Smaller bordered sub-panel widget class (0x5d=93-byte struct, 8 uses -- same size class as Button_Ctor but a distinct vtable/paint). Calls Panel_Ctor's base then sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046eae4). Its paint override (FramedPanel_Paint) is near-identical to TitledPanel_Paint's checkerboard-fill+border logic but without the header-divider-line step -- essentially TitledPanel_Ctor without the titled header, i.e. a plain framed/bordered box.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: FramedPanel_Paint
entries.description: FramedPanel_Ctor's paint override: checkerboard-dithered fill + border, no header-divider lines (compare TitledPanel_Paint). Confirms FramedPanel_Ctor is a plain bordered box.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Grid_Ctor
entries.description: Multi-column grid/list-view widget class (0x6e8=1768-byte struct, 4 uses -- the biggest widget struct in VSHELL by far). Calls Panel_Ctor's base, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ecd8), then initializes 30 fixed row slots (56/0x38 bytes each) via Grid_InitRow, each row holding a 10-column width/flag array (default {14,16} per column). Used by Squad_BuildRosterList and the wcrewi.cpp/wmissini.cpp list screens -- almost certainly the crew/pilot roster and mission objective/weapon lists (30 rows matches a plausible max-crew-slots count).
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Grid_Paint
entries.description: Grid_Ctor's paint override: draws 16px gridlines (both axes) if the grid-lines flag (+0x6e5) is set, then for each of the 30 rows with a non-null icon pointer, blits the row's icon (FUN_00453158) and, for each of its 10 columns whose width differs from the default (0x10), performs a byte-remap-based colour-tint fill (FUN_00457364) over that cell. Conclusively confirms Grid_Ctor is a per-row-icon, per-column-tinted table/list-view widget.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: Grid_InitRow
entries.description: Zeroes one Grid_Ctor row slot (icon ptr, x, y fields) and its 10-column width/flag array to the default {14,16} pair per column. Called 30 times by Grid_Ctor at construction.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, 2026-08-11 VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: maybe_Grid_InitSingleRow
entries.description: Same zero-init pattern as Grid_InitRow but operating on a single standalone row-shaped struct rather than one slot of a Grid_Ctor's 30-row array -- used inline in Mission_BuildScreen's do/while list-building loop. Plausibly a single detached row/line-item struct reusing the same 10-column layout convention, not confirmed against a distinct constructor.

entries.name: HatchedDivider_Ctor
entries.description: Repeating-horizontal-line fill widget class (0x61=97-byte struct, 3 uses -- same size class as maybe_Widget_InitRect but a distinct vtable/paint). Calls Panel_Ctor's base, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ee08), sets width/style fields. Its paint override (HatchedDivider_Paint) draws a repeating stack of horizontal lines from a start offset (+0x55) to the bottom edge, plus an optional small corner-bracket shape if a flag (+0x5d) is set -- looks like a hatched section-divider or scrollbar-track background, not a single separator line.

entries.name: HatchedDivider_Paint
entries.description: HatchedDivider_Ctor's paint override: repeating horizontal-line fill plus an optional corner-bracket shape. Confirms HatchedDivider_Ctor is a hatched/lined fill widget, not a simple 1px separator.

entries.name: ServiceBay_BuildScreen
entries.description: wsrvbayi.cpp (service/repair bay tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref. Every widget's {x,y,w,h} rect is a plain immediate literal in this function (e.g. local_5c=0x27f, local_58=0x1df); no fopen/Volume/ClassIO/fread call anywhere in the function. Confirms VSHELL's tab-screen layouts are hardcoded pixel constants compiled into the EXE, not driven by any data file.

entries.name: Squad_BuildRosterList
entries.description: wsquadi.cpp: builds a repeated row of widgets in a do/while loop over a fixed base rect with a hardcoded per-row Y stride (not a per-row data record). Same TU as Squad_BuildScreen (address range 0043c1a0-0043e52c).

entries.name: Warning_BuildScreen
entries.description: warmingi.cpp (warning screen) builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref. Same hardcoded-rect-literal widget-construction pattern; no file I/O.

entries.name: Crew_BuildScreen
entries.description: wcrewi.cpp (crew tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref. Same hardcoded-rect-literal pattern; no file I/O.

entries.name: Crew_BuildDetailPanel
entries.description: wcrewi.cpp: largest function in the TU (6655 bytes), builds the crew detail/roster panel widget-by-widget with hardcoded rect literals identical in shape to Crew_BuildScreen. Same address range as the wcrewi.cpp TU (00440eb8-00443f33).

entries.name: maybe_Mission_UpdateTerrainLabel
entries.description: wmissini.cpp (mission tab) __FILE__ assert-string anchor function, but small (270 bytes) -- looks up a terrain-description string resource by id and a earth/moon label variant, writes into an existing widget field, not a full screen builder. The real screen builder in this TU is the much larger FUN_00445758 (Mission_BuildScreen).

entries.name: maybe_Mission_UpdateLocationTab
entries.description: wmissini.cpp: small (271 bytes) helper that either loads a fixed-rect bitmap (hardcoded 0x55,0x20,0x3c,0x240,0x168 params) or looks up one of 4 region-label strings by index and updates an existing widget field. Not the main screen builder.

entries.name: Mission_BuildScreen
entries.description: wmissini.cpp: largest function in the TU (4317 bytes), the actual mission-tab screen builder -- same hardcoded-rect-literal widget-construction pattern as the other five screens, plus a do/while loop building a repeated list row with a fixed Y stride. No file I/O.

entries.name: Armory_BuildScreen
entries.description: warmoryi.cpp (armory tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref -- also the largest function in its TU (5365 bytes). Same hardcoded-rect-literal widget-construction pattern; no file I/O. Together with ServiceBay/Squad/Warning/Crew/Mission_BuildScreen, confirms none of VSHELL's tab screens are data-driven -- all layouts are pixel constants compiled into the EXE.

entries.name: ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. Lazy-loads mis_icon.dba, mapshp.dba, and map.dfn into globals (guarded by null-checks), asserts on failure, sets a screen-state byte to 0. Confirmed via direct string references to the three literal filenames.

entries.name: ShellMap_ReleaseResources
entries.description: shellmap.cpp teardown counterpart to ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded -- destroys the 3 loaded resources (calls each object's vtable+0x18 destructor) and nulls the globals. Confirmed the only other reference to ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr in VSHELL.EXE besides the loader -- the loaded DFN panel object's contents are never read, only destroyed.

entries.name: Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper
entries.description: Trivial wrapper funneling .DFN/.HFN panel loads into VshellClassItem_LoadItem with the panel's filename (e.g. "dfn\map.dfn"). VSHELL's own copy of the same wrapper pattern as DBSIM's Panel_LoadWrapper, at a different address since the two EXEs are separate processes.

entries.name: Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper
entries.description: Identical in shape to Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper but for .DBA bitmap-array resources (e.g. "dba\mis_icon.dba"). Confirms both file kinds funnel into the same generic VshellClassItem_LoadItem loader.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_LoadItem
entries.description: classio.cpp, ClassItem::loadItem (confirmed via the literal assert string). VSHELL's own copy of the generic ClassItem registry-dispatch loader -- reads an 8-byte type tag via VshellClassItem_ReadTypeTag, looks up a handler via VshellClassItem_FindHandler, calls its loadFn(stream, mode). Structurally identical to but a separate compiled instance from DBSIM's ClassItem_LoadResource.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_ReadTypeTag
entries.description: Reads the 8-byte type tag ([typeId][0x0028][totalSize]) from a resource stream, called by VshellClassItem_LoadItem. VSHELL's copy of ClassItem_ReadTypeTag.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_FindHandler
entries.description: Searches VSHELL's registry (bucket base VshellClassItem_RegistryBuckets, count-global at 0046d1cc) for a matching type-tag id, returns a 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} descriptor. VSHELL's copy of ClassItem_FindHandler. Note: the registry itself is populated by C++ static initializers at runtime, so it reads as empty/zero in the static binary image -- don't try to walk it directly, trace call graphs from a known class-id literal instead (see VshellPanel_ClassIdGetter).

entries.name: VshellClassItem_RegistryBuckets
entries.description: Base of VSHELL's ClassItem registry bucket array (pairs of {int* entries, int count}, 8 bytes/bucket). Runtime-populated by static initializers -- reads as zero-length in the static image.

entries.name: VshellPanel_ClassIdGetter
entries.description: Trivial getter returning 0x280005, the little-endian dword of the [typeId=5][0x0028] envelope -- confirms vtable 0x0047bf68 is the .DFN/.HFN "Panel" class. Found via ES2FindImmediateRefs literal search across the DBA/DCI/DFN/embedded-bitmap class-id candidates (0x280001/0x280003/0x280005/0x28000b/0x28000e).

entries.name: VshellPanel_Vtable
entries.description: 7-slot vtable for the .DFN/.HFN "Panel" class: +0x00 VshellPanel_ClassIdGetter, +0x04/+0x08 size-calc pair, +0x0c VshellPanel_ReadFromStream, +0x10 VshellPanel_WriteToStream, +0x14 VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType, +0x18 VshellPanel_Destructor. No rendering/accessor methods -- confirms this base class is pure serialization, any consumer must access fields directly rather than through this vtable.

entries.name: VshellPanel_ConstructAndRead
entries.description: The registered factory for class id 0x280005 (called from VshellClassItem_LoadItem via the registry entry's loadFn slot). Allocates a 50 (0x32)-byte object, installs VshellPanel_Vtable, calls vtable+0xc (VshellPanel_ReadFromStream) as obj->readFrom(stream).

entries.name: VshellPanel_ReadFromStream
entries.description: The field-by-field deserializer for the .DFN/.HFN Panel format. Reads 11 int16 fields (struct offsets 0x04-0x18) + 1 int32 (0x1a), then conditionally reads up to 5 variable-length blocks based on those fields' values (3 confirmed present in real files: an offset table, a sparse-byte-value mask pool, a per-record enum byte -- see docs/formats/dfn-hfn-dci.md for the full byte-exact-validated layout). Calls only trivial raw-byte-count stream readers (VshellPanel_ReadInt16/ReadRaw/etc.) -- no field interpretation happens here, semantics were derived from real-file byte inspection instead.

entries.name: VshellPanel_WriteToStream
entries.description: Mirror "save" method of VshellPanel_ReadFromStream -- same field order, confirming the read method's field roles are structural (write and read agree), not just a one-sided guess.

entries.name: VshellPanel_Destructor
entries.description: Frees the up-to-5 conditionally-allocated trailing buffers, then calls the base-class destructor. Vtable+0x18. Confirms 0x0047bf68 is this class's vtable via the self-referential vtable-pointer store (*param_1 = &PTR_FUN_0047bf68).

entries.name: VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType
entries.description: Debug helper (vtable+0x14 on Panel, likely shared shape across other ClassItem-derived classes): calls the object's own classId getter, looks up the registry entry, prints "Class type: %d %d" plus the registry entry's extra field as a %s (suggesting that field is a class-name string, not yet independently confirmed).

entries.name: ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr
entries.description: Global holding the loaded MAP.DFN panel object. Exhaustive address-xref search found only 2 referencing functions in all of VSHELL.EXE -- ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded (the loader) and ShellMap_ReleaseResources (destructor call only). The parsed contents are never read back anywhere in VSHELL -- this specific load is dead/vestigial (the format's real, live consumer is DBSIM's cockpit font system, see ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll).

entries.name: ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll
entries.description: PANEL.CPP-adjacent. Lazy-loads the 18 color-scheme .DFN/.HFN panels (cpblue first, extension chosen by DAT_004d25bb==3) into the ColorSchemePanels array, then the 7 .DCI cursors into a separate array. Loop counts (0x12=18, 7) match the real retail file counts exactly.

entries.name: ColorSchemePanels
entries.description: Base of the 18-element loaded-panel-object array filled by ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll (index 0 = cpblue, per the PTR_s_cpblue_0049b108 name-table iteration order). Unlike VSHELL's dead ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr, this array has 7 real consumer functions in DBSIM.EXE -- each assigns the panel-object pointer wholesale into a widget struct field and passes it as an opaque handle into a generic text/label constructor (FUN_00438920/FUN_00438884) alongside literal display strings, confirming this format is a bitmap FONT resource for DBSIM's cockpit HUD text, not a widget-layout table.

entries.name: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap
entries.description: terrain.cpp. Called by Terrain_LoadZone with the zone's built 'dba\zoneNNNN' path. Also separately loads the shared 'dat\mat0' material/detail-type table (count-prefixed array of 8-byte records, ZONES_MaterialTable) into HeightGrid+0x121. Branches on the path's extension: '.dba' (real retail data, ZONES.VOL\DBA\ZONE*.DBA) goes through ClassItem_LoadResource -> TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap; any other extension falls back to an ASCII fopen/fscanf format ('%d %d %d %d' header = WidthShift/HeightShift/MaxHeightRaw/MinHeightRaw, then one '%d' per cell) -- almost certainly a level-design/debug-only path, no such loose files found in retail data.

entries.name: TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap
entries.description: Real retail terrain loader. Takes a loaded DynamixBitmap (the SAME format used for ordinary .DBM/.DBA textures) and treats its 8-bit grayscale pixel grid directly as the heightmap: WidthShift/HeightShift are re-derived from the bitmap's own width/height fields (log2), each pixel byte (minus a bias param_3) becomes one HeightGrid cell's raw height byte (offset 0), and cell diagonal-select/material-type bits (offset 0xf) are assigned via a weighted random roll (~30.6% chance per material, first match wins) against ZONES_MaterialTable, sparsely at an LOD-driven block stride (finer cells inherit their block's already-rolled material). Verified byte-exact against real ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ZONE*.DBA files: 128x128 zones are 16418 bytes (128*128+34-byte DynamixBitmap header), 256x256 zones are 65570 bytes (256*256+34) -- exact match.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Constructor
entries.description: Zero-initializes a freshly-allocated 0x129-byte HeightGrid (fields +0x3d/+0x3e/+0x3f=0, +0x42=10, +0x43=8 defaults), assigns its vtable. Called once per zone load, right after the FUN_00477390(0x129) allocation in Terrain_LoadZone.

entries.name: Mat0ResourceName
entries.description: Literal string 'mat0' -- resource name for the shared terrain-material table, combined with the 'dat' folder prefix to build 'dat\mat0'. Confirmed against the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/MAT0.DAT.

entries.name: ZoneFilenameTemplate
entries.description: Literal string 'zoneXXXX' -- template overwritten in place by _itoa(zoneIndex) to build each zone's base filename (e.g. 'zone504'). Confirmed against real filenames in ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL (ZONE504.DAT, ZONE504.DBA, etc.).

entries.name: DbaExtensionLiteral
entries.description: Literal string '.dba' -- checked via stricmp in TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap to pick the real-data (ClassItem/DynamixBitmap) loading path over the ASCII fscanf fallback. Confirmed: every real zone heightmap in ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ uses this extension.

entries.name: maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the literal string 'dat' -- used as a folder prefix when building the per-zone header resource path ('dat\zoneNNNN', 16-byte header) and the shared material table path ('dat\mat0'). Confirmed both target files exist for real (ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DAT/ZONE*.DAT, ES2/VOL/simvol0/dat/MAT0.DAT) but the exact path-join semantics of FUN_00492ae0 weren't independently proven beyond this.

entries.name: maybe_DbaFolderPrefix
entries.description: Literal string 'dba' -- used as a folder prefix when building the per-zone heightmap bitmap path ('dba\zoneNNNN.dba'). Confirmed the target files exist for real (ES2/VOL/ZONES.VOL/DBA/ZONE*.DBA) but the exact path-join semantics of FUN_00492ae0 weren't independently proven beyond this.

entries.name: MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts
entries.description: Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout (0x004175dc). Given per-hardpoint slot records (stride 0x1a) and two parallel weapon-id/secondary-key lookup tables, for each occupied slot: reads the weapon id, looks up its WeaponMountTemplate (WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId), reads that template's ProjDatIndex field, resolves the matching PROJ.DAT record (Proj_LookupRecordByIndex direct-index, or Proj_LookupRecord(0,secondaryKey) search for the 0x22 sentinel), then constructs a weapon-id-specific mount C++ object (one of several vtables/sizes keyed by a big switch on the weapon id) passing the resolved template/PROJ.DAT pointers. This is the mech-loadout-time mechanism that resolves a real catalog weapon id into the shot data direct-fire/beam dispatch consumes -- see docs/simulation/dbsim-physics-notes.md and docs/formats/weapons-dat-sim.md.

entries.name: WeaponMountTemplate_GetByWeaponId
entries.description: weaponId * 0x58 + _DAT_004a9970 -- direct flat-array index into the loaded WeaponMountTemplate table (simvol0/dat/WEAPONS.DAT's in-memory copy, 88 bytes/record) by SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog weapon id. Confirms the sim and shell catalogs share one 33-entry order/indexing scheme -- not previously proven, only hypothesized.

entries.name: Proj_LookupRecordByIndex
entries.description: index * 0x24 + ProjDat_RecordTable -- direct flat-array index into PROJ.DAT's in-memory table, distinct from Proj_LookupRecord's (category,subtypeId) linear search. Called by MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts with the value read from a WeaponMountTemplate's ProjDatIndex field, which is what resolves a real catalog weapon id to its PROJ.DAT damage record for 21 of 32 real weapons directly (see Sim.Weapons.WeaponMountTemplate.ProjDatIndex's doc comment for the confirmed full mapping).

entries.name: TSShapeInstance_GetBoundBitmapArray
entries.description: return *(instance + 0x26). Trivial getter for the DBA bitmap-array pointer bound to this specific TSShapeInstance -- confirms texture binding is a per-instance field, not stored in the .DTS file. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSBase_GetActiveBitmapArray
entries.description: return g_ActiveBitmapArray (DAT_005d8010). Paired with TSBase_SetActiveBitmapArray as the only two accessors of that global (confirmed via full xref list). See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSBase_SetActiveBitmapArray
entries.description: g_ActiveBitmapArray = param_1. The only write site for DAT_005d8010 in the whole binary (confirmed via ES2FindAddressRefs on the global's address). See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_ActiveBitmapArray
entries.description: Process-wide 'currently active DBA bitmap-array' pointer. Swapped to a TSShapeInstance's own bound DBA (instance+0x26) for the duration of that instance's render call by TSShapeInstance_Render, then restored. TSBitmapPart_Render indexes into *this* global by BmpTag, not anything owned by the poly's shape. CORRECTION (2026-08-11 UV-formula follow-up): this global is better understood as a 2-field context, not a bare DBA pointer -- *g_ActiveBitmapArray (one deref, offset+0 of what it points to) is the actual DBA object pointer (whose own offset+4=frame count, offset+8=frames pointer-table, confirmed via TSBase::getBitmapPtr's assert), while g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] (a DIFFERENT single deref at offset+4 of g_ActiveBitmapArray's OWN stored value, NOT of the nested DBA object) is a separate pointer to a parallel 20-byte-stride per-frame UV/texture-descriptor table -- see TSTexture4Poly_Render's updated entry. That second field's own builder function was not traced this session (only found via distinguishing instruction-load-count in raw disassembly, not yet reverse engineered further). See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_UseFlatPolyFallback
entries.description: Boolean flag read at the top of TSTexture4Poly_Render, gating which of two ENTIRELY DIFFERENT code paths runs -- NOT 'activeDba pointer-table vs descriptor-table' as an earlier same-session pass claimed (that claim was wrong and is corrected in TSTexture4Poly_Render's own entry). ==0: the REAL scanline-textured path -- builds a per-vertex 3D position array plus a UV-corner array from a 20-byte-stride per-frame descriptor (via g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]), then calls TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA/B. !=0: a flat/solid 2D polygon-fill FALLBACK -- projects+clips the poly's vertices to screen space (FUN_0045e694/FUN_0045ee2c) and fills with FUN_0045f364 (-> FUN_0045f8e7/FUN_0045f8d2), never touching a texture at all, even though it still resolves a DBA frame index via the pointer-table lookup (that resolved value goes unused for actual pixel sampling in this branch -- likely only used for an assert/bounds-check side effect). Exact runtime condition for which value this flag normally holds (a detail-level toggle? a 'texture pack loaded' capability check?) not determined this session.

entries.name: TSBitmapPart_Render
entries.description: Contains the 'TSBase::getBitmapPtr() : index out of range' assert. Reads poly+0x10 (== TSBitmapPart.BmpTag) as a frame index, bounds-checks against g_ActiveBitmapArray's count, looks up g_ActiveBitmapArray.Frames[frameIndex], and if non-null draws a textured quad using poly+0x12/+0x13 (== TSBitmapPart.OfsX/OfsY) for placement. This is the confirmed BmpTag-to-bitmap resolution path. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSShapeInstance_RenderPolys
entries.description: Iterates a shape instance's poly-object list (instance+0x10 = count, instance+0x12 = array base) and calls each poly's own virtual render method (vtable slot +0x1c). Called by TSShapeInstance_Render while g_ActiveBitmapArray is bound to that instance's own DBA. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSShapeInstance_Render
entries.description: Save/swap/restore around TSShapeInstance_RenderPolys: saves g_ActiveBitmapArray, sets it to this instance's own bound DBA (TSShapeInstance_GetBoundBitmapArray), renders all polys, restores the previous global. The core render-time texture-binding entry point. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSShapeInstance_RenderFromRef
entries.description: Near-identical twin of TSShapeInstance_Render, taking the shape instance one level of indirection further (param_1+4) -- same save/swap/restore pattern around g_ActiveBitmapArray. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSBase_LoadDba
entries.description: Prefixes the install-root path onto the given relative .dba path, loads it through VshellClassItem_LoadItem (the same generic Dynamix ClassItem-registry resource loader used for .DFN/.DCI, see project_es2_exe_recon memory). Returns the loaded DBA handle later bound into a TSShapeInstance's +0x26 field or read via array[frame] by TSBitmapPart_Render. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: ESGrid_SetPart
entries.description: Contains the 'ESGrid::setPart out of range' assert (src/esgrid.cpp). Writes a resolved GLBitmap* plus placement fields into one of up to 29 named part slots (0x38-byte stride) on an ESGrid Herc-display widget -- the 2D icon/portrait-painting layer built on top of the base BmpTag mechanism, matching the same 29-part hit-zone indexing used by the mech damage formula. Not needed for base .DTS/.DBA texture rendering, only for VSHELL's per-poly paint-job overlay UI. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_TSObjectTypeRegistry
entries.description: 18-entry, 12-byte-stride table: {tag:uint32 matching TSObjectHeader's on-disk [subtype:u16][supertype:u16] bytes, constructorFnPtr, nameStringPtr}. Confirmed by matching every tag value against Herculan's already-known TSObjectHeader constants (e.g. 0x0014000f = TSTexture4Poly) and the adjacent name strings ("TSPoly", "TSGroup", etc.). This is the DTS-tree node factory VSHELL's/DBSIM's shared ThreeSpace engine uses to construct the right C++ class per on-disk chunk tag -- the reliable way to find any TS*/AN* class's real constructor (and from there its real vtable) when RTTI type-name strings turn out to have zero code references (a recurring dead end in this binary, also seen for .BND's MECH string). One tag (0x0e) has no corresponding entry in TSObjectHeader.cs -- an object type ES2's real .DTS files apparently never use. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_Construct
entries.description: TSTexture4Poly's real constructor, found via g_TSObjectTypeRegistry's tag=0x0014000f entry. Standard Watcom multi-base-class construction pattern: stamps the object's vtable pointer several times (once per base sub-object as each base constructor completes), finishing with &PTR_FUN_0047ee0c -- the actually-used TSTexture4Poly vtable at runtime. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_TSTexture4PolyVtable
entries.description: TSTexture4Poly's real, fully-constructed vtable (found via TSTexture4Poly_Construct's final vtable-pointer stamp, not the dead RTTI string). Slot +0x1c (TSTexture4Poly_Render, FUN_00422af5) is what TSShapeInstance_RenderPolys actually calls for a TSTexture4Poly -- confirming TSTexture4Poly and TSBitmapPart do NOT share one render mechanism, correcting an earlier same-session claim. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_Render
entries.description: TSTexture4Poly's real vtable-slot-0x1c render method (see g_TSTexture4PolyVtable). Stride SETTLED (2026-08-11 follow-up session): reads poly+0xc (ColorIndexId) as MOVZX (unsigned short), SHL 2 (x4) to a byte offset into g_ActiveSurfaceRecords (DAT_005d88a2), then reads front=*(int32*)(base+offset) and back=*(int32*)(base+offset+8) (i.e. +2 int32 slots) -- confirmed via fresh ES2DumpAsm raw disassembly, not just the decompiler. Cross-confirmed independently from DTSModelTransformer.cs's ReadTSGroup/WriteTSGroup, which already read/write the file's group-level surface count as colorCount/4 / Surfaces.Length*4 -- the file format itself encodes surface-related indices in 4-int32-slot units, matching TSSurfaceEntry's true 4-slot (Front/FrontLine/Back/BackLine) layout. CONCLUSION: ColorIndexId = surfaceIndex*4; surfaceIndex = ColorIndexId/4; front value = Surfaces[surfaceIndex].FrontColor, back value = Surfaces[surfaceIndex].BackColor. Front/back is chosen by a visibility test (see TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest) against poly+4/+6. UV-GENERATION FORMULA FOUND (2026-08-11 second follow-up, CORRECTS a wrong claim this entry previously made about g_UseFlatPolyFallback/DAT_00471890): that flag does NOT choose between two texture-lookup styles -- it chooses between the REAL scanline-textured rasterizer (flag==0) and an entirely separate flat/solid 2D polygon-fill FALLBACK (flag!=0, see g_UseFlatPolyFallback's own entry) that never samples a texture at all. Only the flag==0 path reaches TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA/B. In that path, the resolved frame index indexes a 20-byte-stride per-frame descriptor table at g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] (a pointer distinct from the DBA object itself -- see g_ActiveBitmapArray's corrected entry): 4 leading int32 fields F0,F1,F2,F3 (bytes 0-15) plus a 5th field F4 at byte 16 (passed to the rasterizer as param_4, likely a pixel-data pointer/handle). The UV-corner array built for the rasterizer's 4-vertex quad is exactly [V0=(F0,F1), V1=(F2,F1), V2=(F2,F3), V3=(F0,F3)] -- confirmed via decompiled assignment sequence (_DAT_0048a190.._0048a1ac = F0,F1,F2,F1,F2,F3,F0,F3). This is a standard axis-aligned rect-corner mapping (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left in vertex order) IF F0/F1=(left,top) and F2/F3=(right,bottom) of that frame's own texture-space rect. NOT YET TRACED: the builder function that populates g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]'s descriptor table (would settle whether F0-F3 are always a trivial (0,0,width,height) per independently-cropped frame, matching Herculan's existing per-frame DynamixBitmap parsing, or genuine shared-atlas sub-rect coordinates requiring new file/mechanism support) -- a bounded follow-up if resumed, not chased this session per the project's 'don't spend unbounded time on RE before shipping' lesson. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.
entries.source: docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md 2026-08-11, settled 2026-08-11 follow-up, UV formula found 2026-08-11 second follow-up

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolys
entries.description: Render-setup wrapper (implicit-this via unaff_EBP, likely a __thiscall stub or inlined caller) for a TSGroup-like runtime object. Reads iVar1+0x10 (Indexes ptr, default &DAT_005d8014 if null), +0x14 (Points ptr -> DAT_005d8894, confirmed by later x6-byte-stride vertex math matching Vec3Short), +0x18 (Surfaces ptr -> DAT_005d88a2, the 'per-surface runtime record array' TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes), +0x1c (Polys ptr, walked as an array of object pointers), +0x22 (ushort, copied to DAT_005d889c, bounds-checked <1000 and used as a memset-zero byte count for a scratch buffer at DAT_005d88a6 -- matches DTSModelTransformer.cs's on-disk 'colorCount' = Surfaces.Length*4 field exactly, both in field order and in the x4 convention), +0x26 (ushort Polys.Length, loop bound). Loop body calls (*(int*)*polyPtr + 0x1c) i.e. each poly's own vtable slot +0x1c -- matches TSShapeInstance_RenderPolys's documented per-poly render dispatch. Field order (Indexes.Length, Points.Length, colorCount, Polys.Length) is an exact match for TSGroup's on-disk chunk layout as already independently implemented in DTSModelTransformer.cs's ReadTSGroup/WriteTSGroup -- strong two-source confirmation this is TSGroup's own render-time field layout, not merely 'some context object'. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolysFromRef
entries.description: Explicit-param_1 (__cdecl) sibling of TSGroup_RenderPolys (FUN_0042349d) -- identical field reads (param_1+0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x22/0x26) into the same globals, differing only in dispatching the poly walk via FUN_0042362c(param_1,0) instead of an inline loop. Same TSShapeInstance_Render/RenderFromRef-style by-value-vs-by-ref pairing already documented for TSBitmapPart's mechanism. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_ActiveSurfaceRecords
entries.description: Global pointer, set from the active TSGroup-like object's own +0x18 field by TSGroup_RenderPolys/RenderPolysFromRef for the duration of one group's poly walk (save/swap/restore pattern, same shape as g_ActiveBitmapArray). Points at a flat int32[] where surface index k occupies 4 consecutive int32 slots (Front, FrontLine, Back, BackLine), matching TSSurfaceEntry's 8-short/16-byte on-disk layout and DTSModelTransformer.cs's colorCount=Surfaces.Length*4 convention. TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes it at byte offset ColorIndexId*4 (front) and ColorIndexId*4+8 (back), which only lands correctly on a single surface's Front/Back slots if ColorIndexId itself equals surfaceIndex*4 -- confirmed true by the independent file-format cross-check. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA
entries.description: One of two near-identical textured-polygon scanline rasterizer variants called by TSTexture4Poly_Render (dispatched by DAT_00471898), only reached via TSTexture4Poly_Render's g_UseFlatPolyFallback==0 path. Genuine span-based rasterizer: per-edge clipping (FUN_0045c318/c5a4/c6f8), perspective-correct-looking fixed-point interpolation of screen position + a fourth interpolant (lighting or a second UV axis, not yet disambiguated), and inner-loop draw calls (FUN_0045bd58 etc.) -- confirms real (if not yet fully decoded) UV-mapped texturing, not flat shading. UPDATE (2026-08-11 second follow-up): the CALLER's UV-corner-generation formula (what param_2 contains per vertex) is now found -- see TSTexture4Poly_Render's entry. What's still not decoded is this function's OWN internal per-pixel interpolation/sampling math (the fixed-point span-fill loop itself, and the 4th-interpolant's exact semantics) -- not needed to resolve which UV a given vertex gets, only to bit-exactly reproduce the rasterizer's own fill algorithm.
entries.source: docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md 2026-08-11, UV formula found 2026-08-11 second follow-up

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB
entries.description: The other of the two rasterizer variants TSTexture4Poly_Render dispatches between -- longer and does extra sub-span/mip-style step-size selection (DAT_00471980/84/88 thresholds) not present in TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA, suggesting a mipmapped/higher-quality path vs. a simpler one, but not confirmed. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: Called by TSTexture4Poly_Render with poly+4/+6 (Normal/Center vertex-index fields) as arguments; result gates which of a front-color/back-color pair gets used. Reasoned from call-site usage, not independently disassembly-verified instruction-by-instruction the way other 'high' confidence entries in this file are -- worth confirming before relying on the exact facing-test semantics.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupNames
entries.description: 7-entry array of pointers to the literal strings 'light'/'medium'/'heavy'/'enemy'/'apocatex'/'razortex'/'newhercs' (the strings themselves start at 0049a437, 0x0049a37c holds an 8th unrelated pointer -- not part of this array, unresearched). Confirmed dead in DBSIM.EXE's own code (zero xrefs to the array base or any individual string, checked both via ReferenceManager and a full-binary decompiled-text scan) -- DBSIM does NOT read this table at runtime to pick a mech's DBA. The real runtime mechanism is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry) feeding g_MechTextureGroupSlots directly; this string table is very likely leftover linked-in rodata from the same shared ThreeSpace source file, present in the binary but never actually executed. Byte-verified against Herculan/docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md's already-known 7-name set from VSHELL/user domain knowledge -- exact match.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupSlots
entries.description: 8-byte-stride array, one slot per texture group (light/medium/heavy/enemy/apocatex/razortex/newhercs -- see g_MechTextureGroupNames, though this array is populated independently of that dead string table; the loader that fills each slot from a real .DBA wasn't traced this session). MechType_InitOne (0041a8) writes '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + textureGroupIndex*8' directly into every mesh sub-component's TSShapeInstance+0x26 (the confirmed bound-active-DBA field from docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md's VSHELL RE) at mech-spawn time -- this is the actual, confirmed, executed mech-to-texture-atlas binding mechanism in DBSIM.EXE.

entries.name: MechType_InitOne
entries.description: Per-mech-type init, called once per valid slot (0-0x54) by Mechs_InitAllTypes. Opens the per-mech-type resource files (name built from the mech's own code string + several folder-prefix globals), reads a 0xd8-byte fixed record into the MECH_TYPE_DATA[typeIndex] struct (0x21e bytes/entry) at record offset 2, initializes hit-zone/collision/debris sub-resources, and -- the confirmed answer to 'how does DBSIM pick a mech's texture' -- for every mesh sub-component of this mech type, sets TSShapeInstance+0x26 (bound active DBA, see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md) to '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + typeRecord[0x96]*8'. typeRecord+0x96 is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry); the 0xd8-byte record it lives in is read directly from simvol0/dat/<MECHNAME>.DAT, byte-exact match with HercWorks.Core's already-ported (but previously unregistered) HercSimDat/HercSimDataTransformer -- offset 0x96 in the record = offset 148 in the file = HercSimDat.ModelSkinId, which the original Java port had already named correctly without knowing why.

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: Creates the 'mechs' object pool (string xref confirmed) sized DAT_004a9d8a*0x21e (the MECH_TYPE_DATA record size), then loops mech-type slot 0..0x54 calling MechType_InitOne (004201a8) for every slot MechTypeSlot_GetIndex (0041ff00) reports as in-use (!= 0xff).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex
entries.description: Trivial accessor, returns (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] -- a per-slot byte, 0xff sentinel meaning 'unused', otherwise the allocated dense index used by MechType_InitOne. Not independently cross-checked beyond its two callers (Mechs_InitAllTypes, MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate
entries.description: Assigns the next dense allocation index (DAT_004a9d8a, post-incremented) to slot param_1's (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] entry the first time it's requested; on the very first allocation overall, also caches an object-pool handle (FUN_0040feb4(1) result) into _DAT_004a9df4. Not independently cross-checked beyond call-site usage.

entries.name: HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte
entries.description: Writes the HeightGrid's parallel per-cell scratch/flag byte array at +0xf0: derives the cell index from a cell pointer as ((cellPtr - grid[+0xec]) >> 4) and stores param_3 there. Called once per cell by TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap with 0; the ASCII fallback loader writes the same array inline instead. Identifies the +0xf0 array's writer -- its *consumer* is still unlocated, so what the byte means remains open.

entries.name: Math_RandomNext
entries.description: The game's pseudo-random generator: an additive lagged Fibonacci generator over a 56-entry (0x38) table of shorts with two rotating byte cursors at state+0x70 and state+0x71. Each call does table[i] += table[j]; returns the new table[i] in the low 16 bits; then advances both cursors modulo 56. Callers pass the state block address (0x4d261d) and mask the result -- & 0xfff for the terrain material roll in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and for the explosion's ~51% per-component roll in FUN_004187d0. The 56 seed values live in the data section and have not been extracted.

entries.name: Cpp_VectorNew
entries.description: The compiler's C++ 'vector new' runtime helper (carries the 'Illegal mode in vector new' error string): optionally allocates param_2*param_3 bytes (plus a 4-byte count prefix when mode bit 0x10 is set), then invokes the element constructor param_5 once per element at param_2 stride. Worth having named because it appears in the middle of data-structure loaders -- e.g. the HeightGrid cell array allocation in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap -- where it can otherwise be mistaken for domain logic.

entries.name: HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch
entries.description: Single-statement function: memsets the HeightGrid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch byte array to 0, sized (1 << grid[+0x100]) * (1 << grid[+0x104]) -- i.e. exactly one byte per cell, using the same width/height shift fields the rest of the terrain code uses. Called first thing in Scene_SubmitFrameObjects, so the +0xf0 array is per-frame working state (reset every frame), not persistent zone data. Pairs with HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68), which writes it. Its READER is still unlocated -- what the byte actually means remains open.

entries.name: maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects
entries.description: Per-frame scene assembly. Calls HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch(ActiveHeightGrid) first, then walks ~10 separate global object lists (the flat/flat2 ground shapes from maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes' list at 004a9711, GlobalMechList, and eight others), calling a small per-object submit helper (004282d8 / 0042837c / 004283b4) on each and caching a 2-byte result pair into each object at +0x7a / +0x1ea. Named 'maybe_' because the per-object helpers were not decoded, so 'submit for render' vs. some other per-frame pass is inferred from position and structure, not proven.

entries.name: maybe_Terrain_ComputeViewDistance
entries.description: LOCATES THE CONSUMER OF THE HeightGrid LOD FIELD (+0x10c), previously recorded as unlocated. Converts the viewer position (param_2+4/+8) to cell coordinates by >> cellShift (+0x108), then computes grid[+0x10c] << cellShift -- the LOD field scaled from cells into world units. If the viewer's cell is within LOD cells of any grid edge (tested against both 1 << grid[+0x100] and 1 << grid[+0x104]) that distance collapses to a literal 1000. Then builds a transform from the viewer's angle (+0x14) plus grid[+0x110] and emits two values into param_3. Called once per frame from 0042e700 with ActiveHeightGrid, writing into the world object at +0x72. Named 'maybe_' because the final three-call chain (00480330 / 0048c4f0 / 0048c5c4) was not decoded, so 'view/draw distance' is the reading most consistent with the arithmetic and the edge clamp, not a proven semantic for the two outputs.

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
